chapter: Family and the lake excursion boats
title: No brass bands across the lake
summary: Madisonville seldom had brass bands, only occasional Labor Day parades. Local music was mostly Dixieland and string bands.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Speaking of across the lake, is there anything else you can tell us about the early music over there? Were there any brass bands for parades over there?
Well, they had one or two bands came over there on the Labor Day to parade for the Labor Day parade, but that wasn't every year. and then they could get somebody.
You didn't have any brass bands like the Fritz band, those fellows?
No, no, no, it was mostly Dixieland bands, strings bands, you know what I call it.
You couldn't hardly get a band to go around there. It was so hard to get.
Here I was so tied up, see. That's what would be the thing.
So the only parade you saw were the bands from here.
That's right. After I come here, yeah. The border of July,
Labor Day, you couldn't get no bands. Everybody was tied up.
